dct_description_sm: The Wildlife Research section conducts scientific research and wildlife monitoring programs involving the collection, analysis, application and archiving of both scientific data and Inuit knowledge related to wildlife. Development of management plans, regulations, and conservation recommendations for consideration by the Nunavut Wildlife Management Board (NWMB) are achieved through extensive community and stakeholder consultation. The purpose of the Caribou Health Monitoring (CHM) program is to establish and evaluate a hunter-based program of information and sample collection for health monitoring and genetic analysis of caribou. This research addresses key wildlife concerns of local HTOs and wildlife managers while providing an opportunity for hunters and scientists to combine their knowledge and resources for the benefit of caribou. The goals of this program include the establishment of baseline values for health parameters and genetic diversity, with the potential for long-term monitoring to detect future change
